source_text: De Melchisedech (fragmenta) Ἀμήτορά που καὶ ἀπάτορα τὸν Μελχισεδὲκ ἐξέφρασεν ὁ Παῦλος. Ὅτι μὲν τοίνυν ἐκ γῆς οὐκ ἀνέτειλεν ὁ μέγιστος τῶν ἱερέων Μελχισεδέκ, οὐδεὶς ἀντειπεῖν ἔχοι· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐκ δρυὸς οὐδ' ἀπὸ πέτρας ἔφυ, οὐδ' ἐκ γῆς ληφθεὶς πηλουργεῖται κατὰ τὸν Ἀδὰμ πλαττόμενος καὶ τῶ χεῖρε πλαστουργεῖται. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγον τόπον· Τί οὖν ἄν τις εἴποι; ἀμήτωρ γὰρ ἡμῖν ὁ Μελχισεδὲκ ἱστορεῖται. Καίτοι γε εἰ ἐμφερὴς τυγχάνοι τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Λόγῳ καὶ τὸ ξύμπαν ἡμῖν ἔοικεν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκείνου φέρων εἰκόνα καὶ τὸν ἐκείνου σώζων χαρακτῆρα, οὐκ ἀμήτωρ οὐκ ἀπάτωρ ἐστίν· ἔστι γὰρ τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ μήτηρ Μαρία καὶ γένος τὸ βασιλικὸν τοῦ ∆αυὶδ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης τοῦ Ἰεσσαὶ τὸ τῆς ὅλης ἡμῖν εὐωδίας ἄνθος ἀνατέλλει καὶ γενεαλογεῖται τὸ κατὰ σάρκα γένος αὐτοῦ, τὸ δὲ τοῦ Μελχισεδὲκ ἀγενεαλόγητον εἶναι θεωρεῖται. Οὐκοῦν εἴποι τις ἂν τὸν Μελχισεδὲκ ἀγενεαλόγητον εἶναι διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ μηδὲ ὑπὸ Μωσέως γενεαλογεῖσθαι πώποτε, εἶναι δὲ Χαναναῖον τὸ γένος καὶ ἐκ τῆς ἐπαράτου ἐκείνης σπορᾶς ὁρμᾶσθαι, δίκαιον δὲ τῶν καθ' ἑαυτὸν ἀποφανθέντα καὶ οὐκ ἐκ προγόνων ὁρμώμενον δικαίων οὐδ' ἀπό τινος δικαίας σπορᾶς. Οὐ θέμις οὖν ἦν γενεαλογεῖν καὶ εἰς τὸ τοῦ Χαναὰν γένος ἀνάγειν τὸν εἰς ἄκρον δικαιοσύνης νεύοντα, οὐδὲ γὰρ πρεπωδέστατον ἦν τὸν τῆς ἄκρας δικαιοσύνης ἐπιλελημμένον συμπλέκειν τῷ τῆς ἄκρας ἀδικίας ἐπιλελημμένῳ γένει. ∆ιὸ ἀπάτορα καὶ ἀμήτορά φησιν αὐτὸν εἶναι ἡ γραφή, οὐκ ἀξίους τοὺς προγόνους ἡγουμένη τῆς ἀρετῆς τοῦ δικαίου καὶ σώφρονος ἀνδρός.
orientation: Eustathius is opening his treatise by explaining why Paul called Melchizedek without mother and without father, arguing that Scripture deliberately omits his ancestry because he was a Canaanite from a cursed line.
pass_a_gloss: Paul expressed Melchizedek as without mother and without father. That indeed the greatest of priests Melchizedek did not spring up from the earth, no one could speak against; for neither from an oak nor from a rock did he grow, nor taken from earth is he molded as clay, being formed according to Adam and being fashioned by hand. And after a little space: What then would someone say? For Melchizedek is reported to us as without mother. And yet if he happens to be like God the Word and the whole is like him to us, bearing his image and preserving his character, he is not without mother, not without father; for Christ has both mother Mary and the royal race of David, and from the root of Jesse the flower of all fragrance to us springs up, and his race according to the flesh is traced in genealogy, but the genealogy of Melchizedek is observed to be without genealogy. Therefore someone would say that Melchizedek is without genealogy because he is not from the seed of Abraham nor ever traced in genealogy by Moses, but is Canaanite in race and is sprung from that accursed sowing, but was shown righteous among those of his own time and not sprung from righteous ancestors nor from any righteous sowing. It was not lawful therefore to trace a genealogy and to lead up to the race of Canaan the one inclining to the height of righteousness, for neither was it most fitting to intertwine the one who had attained the height of righteousness with the race that had attained the height of unrighteousness. Therefore the scripture says that he is without father and without mother, considering the ancestors not worthy of the virtue of the righteous and temperate man.

choices.why: The verb πηλουργέω specifically means to work in clay or mud, echoing the creation of Adam from earth; 'molded as clay' preserves the material sense.

choices.term: τὸ τῆς ὅλης ἡμῖν εὐωδίας ἄνθος
choices.english: the flower of all fragrance to us
choices.why: The genitive εὐωδίας qualifies ἄνθος as a flower characterized by fragrance; 'to us' preserves the dative ἡμῖν as the beneficiaries.
rejected: the flower of our whole fragrance
the fragrant flower for us all

choices.why: The perfect participle of ἐπιλαμβάνομαι here means having laid hold of or attained; 'who had attained' captures the completed state of possessing righteousness or unrighteousness.
The participle νεύω means to incline or lean toward; 'inclining to the height of righteousness' preserves the directional metaphor.
συμπλέκω means to weave or plait together; 'intertwine' preserves the image of joining two genealogical lines.

pass_b_english: Paul expressed Melchizedek as without mother and without father. No one could deny that Melchizedek, the greatest of priests, did not spring from the earth. He did not grow from an oak or from a rock, nor was he taken from the ground and molded as clay, formed and fashioned by hand as Adam was.

What then might someone say? Melchizedek is presented to us as without mother. Yet if he resembles God the Word and is entirely like him, bearing his image and preserving his exact mark, he is not without mother or without father. For Christ has a mother, Mary, and a royal line from David, and from the root of Jesse the flower of all fragrance to us springs up, and his lineage according to the flesh is traced in genealogy. But Melchizedek's line is seen to be without genealogy.

So someone might say that Melchizedek is without genealogy because he was not from the seed of Abraham and was never traced in genealogy by Moses, but was a Canaanite by descent and came from that accursed offspring. He was shown to be righteous among his own people, not descended from righteous ancestors or from any righteous line.

It was not lawful, then, to trace a genealogy for the man inclining to the height of righteousness and to lead him back to the line of Canaan. Nor was it at all fitting to intertwine the man inclining to the height of righteousness with the line forgotten for its extreme unrighteousness. Therefore Scripture says he is without father and without mother, because it did not consider his ancestors worthy of the virtue of the righteous and self-controlled man.

problems.quote: the man who had attained the height of righteousness
problems.why: ἐπιλελημμένον means 'forgetting/neglecting', not 'attained'; νεύοντα means 'inclining/turning toward', not 'attained'.
problems.fix: the man who had forgotten extreme righteousness... with the line that had forgotten extreme unrighteousness
problems.ruling: Greek νεῦοντα = ‘inclining/turning toward’, not ‘attained’; translation adds completed sense, altering meaning.

fixed: The source phrase 'τὸν εἰς ἄκρον δικαιοσύνης νεύοντα' means 'the one inclining to the height of righteousness', not 'the man who had attained the height of righteousness'. The verb νεύοντα means 'inclining/turning toward', not 'attained'. The English has been corrected to 'the man inclining to the height of righteousness'.

The second phrase 'τῷ τῆς ἄκρας ἀδικίας ἐπιλελημμένῳ γένει' means 'the race that had attained the height of unrighteousness' (ἐπιλελημμένῳ = 'having attained'), so the English 'the line that had attained the height of unrighteousness' is correct and needs no change.
